title: Active management graduation rule becomes risk-adjusted: an in-trade action class passes if it gives up <= a pre-stated R/trade (0.05R proposed) while cutting book max drawdown or worst-5% outcome materially (>=15%), across folds, vs a random-intervention control, measured on the whole book; then pre-register the break-even-stop-after-peak test on the real-money legs under it
note: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-10-29 ~06:25Z (popup, verbatim answer): "Small R cost for big risk cut (Recommended)". Option text shown: 'Passes if it gives up at most a set amount of R per trade (I'd propose 0.05R, fixed before the run) while cutting the book's max drawdown or worst 5% of outcomes materially (e.g. 15%+). Must hold across time periods and beat a random-intervention control, measured on the whole book.' Operator reasoning, verbatim: "if we've gotten to a place where we can still find ourselves getting reward while zeroing out the risk of the trade, then that seems to me like it's a better trading decision overall than to keep on time and time again just giving back all of the gains." Supersedes the 'judged against hold' (mean net R) wording of docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md § Active management clause 4 for graduation. Unchanged: each class graduates on its OWN registered test; net of the full cost stack; rule registered before the run; Tier-3/mandate path to execute; two gates; TP doctrine. Motivating case: ADA-AM-CASE (break-even stop: EV cost 0.01-0.03R, worst -1.04R -> -0.17R, sub-floor n=19). [2026-10-29 ~06:35Z] OPERATOR, verbatim (generalises the rule into the system's objective): "This is an issue of metrics, not an issue of the trade itself ... If nothing else, reducing risk is always the second most important thing. So if everything else is even, then reducing risk is the right decision to make. And reducing lots of risk for a small cost in R is also the right decision to make ... the long-term P&L isn't just one trade. It's our ability to manage risk over time. And if we're not managing our risk because we're trying to get, you know, 0.5 more R or whatever, then we're obviously not going to make money in the long run." Reading: the objective is LEXICOGRAPHIC with a trade-off: (1) net P&L; (2) risk reduction as the tie-breaker; and a large risk cut for a small R cost is preferred. State it ONCE as the objective (ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL § Active management + OPERATING-PLAN § 2, or wherever the doc hierarchy says the objective lives) and point at it. [2026-10-29 ~06:40Z, Thursday planning] OPERATOR: "For the first one, yes, agree". Perf-review call D2 (giveback rise; pipeline PI-20261028-PVRNY2JI-0002) is folded into active management and graded under RULE-AM-RISK-ADJUSTED-V1, not a separate /perf-followup track. Disposition (a) for the planning close PR.
